key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate task-specific predictions, while multitask neural networks provided strong shared-learning performance across the related welding outputs.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between a shared-model approach for correlated quality metrics and a higher-accuracy ensemble approach for individual property prediction.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding properties: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated both models using RMSE and R² on the same shared dataset.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² for all three targets in most cases, with especially strong results for UTS (RMSE 0.0263, R² 0.9863) and weld hardness (RMSE 0.0467, R² 0.9782).
watch_item: Performance is reported on a shared dataset, so practical deployment should verify generalization on new welding conditions, materials, and process settings.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
